audit.report: A replayable batch job (batch_replayable_inventory, pid 14138) held an idle transaction for 4 seconds, blocking one session and causing checkout success to collapse from 92% to 45% with $10,052/min revenue at risk. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker; the Continuity Guardian accepted after trade-off analysis showed waiting would cost ~$150,108 (896s remaining) versus a 4-minute replay cost. The authority authorized the termination, the executor killed the session, and the verifier confirmed full recovery: zero lock waits, 100% checkout success over 10s, and no protected settlements affected. Total negotiation and execution took 59.7 seconds, within the 60-second business tolerance.
audit.root_cause: An idle-in-transaction batch_replayable_inventory worker (pid 14138) blocked checkout sessions, driving success rate below SLO.
lessons: Add a statement_timeout or idle_in_transaction_session_timeout for batch_replayable_inventory workers so they self-terminate before blocking checkout.
Pre-register batch_replayable_inventory in the change calendar with an explicit may_interrupt window to eliminate the calendar probe round.
Instrument batch_replayable_inventory to emit a heartbeat or checkpoint metric so the detector can flag stalls before they become blockers.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian proposed the correct action in round 1 with full evidence (lock wait, business impact, replayability, memory precedent); the Continuity Guardian accepted immediately with no objections or conditions. No rounds were wasted and no guardian missed evidence or was overridden by an invariant.
follow_ups: Implement idle-in-transaction timeout for batch_worker role targeting batch_replayable_inventory.
Add batch_replayable_inventory to the change calendar with a standing may_interrupt window.
Add a liveness probe / heartbeat metric to the inventory_reconcile job for earlier stall detection.
